text: Supports infrastructure definition in TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, .NET, Java, YAML, and HCL with full provider coverage in each language
quote: Pulumi supports TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, .NET, Java, YAML, and HCL. Each language is equally capable and supports the full surface area of all Pulumi Registry providers.

text: Automation API lets you run Pulumi programs programmatically without invoking the CLI
quote: The Pulumi Automation API is a programmatic interface for running Pulumi programs without the Pulumi CLI.

text: Provides unit, property, and integration testing capabilities for infrastructure code, including in-memory mocked unit tests
quote: Unit Tests are fast in-memory tests that mock all external calls. Property Tests run resource-level assertions while infrastructure is being deployed. Integration Tests deploy ephemeral infrastructure and run external tests against it.

text: Supports storing state either in Pulumi Cloud's managed backend or in a self-managed object store (S3, Azure Blob, GCS)
quote: Pulumi supports two classes of state backend: Pulumi Cloud... DIY backend: a “Do It Yourself” backend that stores state in an object store you manage—AWS S3, Azure Blob Storage, Google Cloud Storage...

text: Policy-as-code framework to define and enforce guardrails across resources managed by Pulumi, Terraform, CloudFormation, or created manually
quote: Pulumi Policies enables you to implement policy as code across your entire cloud infrastructure. You define guardrails in code and apply them consistently across resources managed by Pulumi IaC, provisioned with Terraform or CloudFormation,

text: Can import an existing cloud resource into Pulumi state and auto-generate the matching program code to manage it
quote: you run `pulumi import` against a specific cloud resource. Pulumi adds the resource to your stack’s state and generates the code needed to manage it, which you then copy into your Pulumi program.

text: Can generate an import file listing all resources a program would create, for review before bulk-importing
quote: run `pulumi preview --import-file` to generate an import file listing every resource the program would otherwise create

text: Official MCP server lets AI assistants query Pulumi Cloud stacks and search across managed cloud resources
quote: Pulumi’s MCP server implementation provides AI assistants with the ability to: Query your Pulumi Cloud stacks and their resources, Search across all cloud resources...

text: MCP server also lets AI coding assistants generate infrastructure code and delegate tasks to the Neo agent
quote: The Pulumi Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enables AI-powered coding assistants to access your Pulumi Cloud resources, generate infrastructure code, and optionally delegate tasks to Pulumi Neo.

text: Can preview exactly what changes (creates/updates/deletes) a deployment will make without applying them
quote: Show a preview of updates to a stack’s resources... No changes to the stack will actually take place.

text: Neo is a built-in AI agent that provisions, governs, and optimizes cloud infrastructure with enterprise controls
quote: Neo provisions, governs, and optimizes your cloud infrastructure — with enterprise controls built in.

text: Provides guided migration path from Terraform, CloudFormation, and other IaC tools
quote: Migrate from Terraform, CloudFormation, and other tools.

text: Offers self-service infrastructure via templates, guardrails, and a developer portal
quote: Self-service infrastructure with templates, guardrails, and developer portals.

text: Lets infrastructure be authored using standard general-purpose language features like loops, functions, classes, and package managers instead of YAML
quote: Skip the YAML, and use standard language features like loops, functions, classes, and package management that you already know and love.

text: Provides Pulumi-maintained version control integrations for GitHub, GitLab, and Azure DevOps
quote: Connect Pulumi with GitHub, GitLab, and Azure DevOps using Pulumi-maintained version control integrations.

text: Unit tests are written in the same language as the Pulumi program and can use familiar test/mock frameworks like Mocha or NUnit
quote: Unit tests are authored in the same language as the Pulumi program under test. You can use your favorite test and mock frameworks like Mocha for Node.js or NUnit for .NET.

text: Most IaC projects require bringing existing resources (from other tools or manual creation) under management, which Pulumi supports
quote: Most infrastructure as code projects require working with existing cloud resources, whether those resources were originally created with another IaC tool or manually provisioned

text: MCP server integrates with multiple AI coding tools including Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf, and Claude Desktop
quote: The Pulumi MCP server works with various AI-powered development tools: **Cursor**...**Anthropic’s Claude Code**...**Windsurf**...**Claude Desktop**

text: Neo can be instructed in plain English to handle dependencies, execute changes, and monitor outcomes automatically
quote: Tell Neo what you need in plain English. It handles dependencies, executes changes, and monitors outcomes automatically.

text: Backend options include a managed Pulumi Cloud service or simple object storage in AWS S3, Azure Blob Storage, or Google Cloud Storage
quote: Backend options include Pulumi Cloud, an easy-to-use, secure, and reliable hosted application ... in addition to simple object storage in AWS S3, Microsoft Azure Blob Storage, Google Cloud Storage

text: Pulumi can be self-hosted
quote: Self-hosting available

text: Automatically provisions and manages resources across AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, and 300+ providers
quote: Pulumi automatically provisions and manages your resources on AWS, Azure, Google Cloud Platform, Kubernetes, and 300+ providers
